question: Who provided the earliest form of organized care in infirmaries and almshouses?
explanation: Monks and nuns established early infirmaries and almshouses to shelter the sick and poor. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why was early healthcare considered a communal responsibility?

options.B: Traditional healers charged fixed daily wages
options.C: Governments forced citizens to build clinics
options.D: Families and elders managed illnesses collectively

explanation: Before modern facilities, communities relied on collective knowledge and family caregiving structures. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h1)

question: What factor drove the rapid expansion of district nursing during the Industrial Revolution?

options.A: The discovery of safe synthetic antibiotics
options.B: A surplus of trained medical doctors
options.C: Severe overcrowding and infectious disease outbreaks
options.D: Strict government mandates on hospital building

explanation: Urbanization and poor living conditions created massive disease burdens that factories and early hospitals could not manage. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h2)

question: What was the main contribution of Lillian Wald to public health nursing?

options.A: Writing the initial hospital sanitation codes
options.B: Discovering the germ theory of disease

explanation: Lillian Wald founded the Henry Street Settlement in New York, which advanced public health nursing and social welfare. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h2)

question: What was the primary focus of early Western healthcare during the colonial era in Nigeria?

options.B: Providing free surgery for all citizens

explanation: Initial colonial health efforts prioritized the survival and productivity of administration staff and military personnel. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h3)

question: How did healthcare delivery expand to local populations in early Nigerian history?

options.A: By establishing private health insurance companies
options.C: By closing all traditional healing centres
options.D: Through mission clinics and government dispensaries

explanation: Missionaries and colonial administrations gradually set up local dispensaries and clinics outside major administrative stations. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which international declaration established Primary Health Care as the key strategy for global health?
explanation: The 1978 Alma-Ata Declaration emphasized health as a fundamental human right and prioritized primary health care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h4)

question: What was the main philosophical shift brought by the Primary Health Care movement?

options.A: Focusing treatment exclusively on urban workers
options.B: Relying entirely on advanced surgical interventions
options.C: Moving from expensive hospital care to community prevention
options.D: Transferring all health funding to private investors

explanation: Primary health care redirected resources and attention toward accessible, community-based prevention rather than curative hospital care alone. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge currently facing Nigerian community health nursing?

options.C: Complete elimination of all infectious diseases
options.D: Shortages of staff due to international migration

explanation: Infectious diseases remain a significant burden in Nigeria, meaning they have not been completely eliminated. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h5)

question: How do modern community health nurses help mitigate staff shortages in Nigerian primary facilities?

options.A: By closing rural clinics to concentrate in cities
options.B: By implementing task-shifting policies with trained workers
options.C: By replacing all nurses with automated machines
options.D: By refusing to treat non-emergency patients

explanation: Task-shifting allows certain responsibilities to be shared safely with trained community health extension workers to maximize coverage. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h5)
